title: Article 391 — Power of the President to amend the First and Fourth Schedules in certain contingencies (Omitted)

content.overview: Article 391 empowered the President to amend the First and Fourth Schedules in certain transitional contingencies between the passing and commencement of the Constitution. Omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956). Spent; not living law.
content.glance: Art 391 omitted by 7th Amendment 1956 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956). Transitional Schedule-amendment power — spent.
content.study: Part of the 379–391 transitional block. Omitted by 7th Amendment, 1956 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956). Living amendment of Schedules is under Article 4 (for Arts 2/3 laws) and the ordinary amendment process where applicable.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Status of Article 391?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Omitted by the 7th Amendment, 1956 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956). Spent transitional provision.

examTips: Group with Arts 379–391; living Schedule changes via Art 4 / ordinary amendment.

examples.title: Application of art-391
examples.body: Facts that satisfy the elements stated in the provision produce the consequence described in the text.

hypotheticals.question: Do the facts engage art-391?
hypotheticals.analysis: Compare the facts with the statutory or constitutional elements stated in the text.

distinctions.title: Scope of art-391
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the constitutional text.

misconceptions.myth: art-391 creates unlimited or extra-textual rights.
misconceptions.correction: It operates only as stated in the constitutional provision.
